_comment: A worked STANDARD Implementation Contract v1 (docs/impl-contract.md).
It lives on a task as `metadata.impl_contract`. This example is
deliberately a STATEFUL task, because that is where the gate earns its
keep: it carries a source_of_truth and a state_model, one HIGH decision
that analysis actually resolved, one MEDIUM decision legitimately
deferred with a default AND a guardrail, and two LOW decisions handed to
the coding agent. `enforcement` is `advisory` -- the v1 rollout default:
This `_comment` key is itself a demonstration: it is not a v1 field,
so the gate reports UNKNOWN_FIELD against it -- non-blocking, because a
field is reported rather than dropped in silence. The contract is READY.
goal: A worker crash must free its claimed task within one lease TTL instead of stranding it in RUNNING forever.
current_behavior: queue_tasks.claim_token/lease_expires_at are stamped at claim time but nothing ever reads lease_expires_at back, so a task whose worker died stays RUNNING until a human notices and re-assigns it by hand.
expected_behavior: A task whose lease has expired and whose worker has not renewed is returned to READY with attempt_count unchanged, and the release is recorded with a reason so it is distinguishable from a voluntary release.
source_of_truth: the queue_tasks table (sqlite). Every board/fleet view already derives from it; the in-memory engine state is a cache and is rebuilt from it on restart.

state_model.writer: queue_store, inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE -- no other module writes these columns

invariants: a task is claimed by at most one worker at a time (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, unchanged)
attempt_count is incremented only on dispatch, never on a lease release
a COMPLETED or FAILED task is never re-opened by expiry

assumptions.statement: lease_expires_at is always written in UTC by every existing claim path
a worker that is alive but merely slow will renew within the TTL
assumptions.guardrail: every expiry release is logged with the last renewal age; a release whose age is under 2x TTL is an alertable signal that the TTL is too short, not a normal event

assumptions.statement: no dashboard view caches RUNNING state longer than its poll interval

edge_cases: clock moved backwards between claim and expiry check
the worker renews in the same tick the sweeper decides to expire it
a task released by expiry is immediately re-claimed by the same worker that had it
dangerous_failure_modes: releasing a task whose worker IS alive, so two workers edit the same tree -- this is the window/window2 transcript-collision class of incident
double-incrementing attempt_count on release, which silently burns the task's retry budget
expiring a task that is already COMPLETED and re-dispatching finished work
acceptance: a task whose lease_expires_at is in the past and whose worker has not renewed returns to READY within one sweep
attempt_count is unchanged across the release
a renewed lease is never released
the release row records reason=LEASE_EXPIRED and the last renewal age
live_verify: claim a task on a disposable lane, SIGKILL the worker's tmux session, and watch the task return to READY on the real dashboard within one TTL -- not just the unit test
out_of_scope: the handoff verb (P0.4's own separate item)

context_pack.why: the BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim pattern this must not break
the renewal model to copy; already pane_key-generic
why this exists and what was deliberately left out
where the queue-state assertions already live

decision_budget.question: On expiry, does the task go back to READY or to UNASSIGNED?
decision_budget.decision: READY, keeping its session binding. UNASSIGNED would drop the project/session affinity that routing already paid for, and a crashed worker is usually restarted on the same node.

decision_budget.question: Who runs the expiry sweep -- the engine tick, or a dedicated loop?
decision_budget.default: the existing engine tick, so there is no new process and no new failure mode
decision_budget.guardrail: the sweep must be O(expired), bounded per tick, and must log when it hits its own bound -- a sweep that silently truncates is worse than no sweep

decision_budget.question: What is the log message wording for a lease release?
Does the sweeper live in queue_store or queue_engine?
decision_budget.default: wherever the surrounding transaction already is
